cases.sentence: Однажды сыновья Божии пришли, чтобы предстать перед ___, и Сатана пришел с ними.
cases.translation: One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came with them.
cases.explain: The preposition 'перед' (before) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Господь сказал Сатане: 'Я видел твою непорочность, но ты настраивал меня против него, чтобы погубить его без ___.'
cases.translation: The Lord said to Satan: 'I saw his integrity, but you incited me against him to destroy him without cause.'
cases.explain: The preposition 'без' (without) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Сатана ответил: 'Кожа за кожу, и за свою жизнь человек отдаст все, что имеет, но протяни руку и порази его ___.'
cases.translation: Satan answered: 'Skin for skin, and for his own life a man will give all he has, but stretch out your hand and strike his bones.'
cases.explain: The verb 'порази' (strike) governs the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Господь сказал Сатане: 'Хорошо, он в твоих ___, только сохрани ему жизнь.'
cases.translation: The Lord said to Satan: 'Very well, he is in your hands, only spare his life.'
cases.explain: The preposition 'в' (in) governs the prepositional case when referring to location.

cases.sentence: Сатана ушел от Господа и поразил Иова болезненными язвами с головы до ___.
cases.translation: Satan left the presence of the Lord and struck Job with painful sores from head to foot.
cases.explain: The preposition 'до' (to/until) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Тогда Иов взял черепок от глиняной посуды, чтобы скоблить себя им, и сел в ___.
cases.translation: Then Job took a potsherd to scrape himself with it, and sat down in ashes.
cases.explain: The preposition 'в' (in) governs the prepositional case for location.

cases.sentence: Жена сказала ему о его ___, но Иов отказался проклинать Бога.
cases.translation: His wife spoke to him of his suffering, but Job refused to curse God.
cases.explain: The preposition 'о' (about) governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Когда трое друзей услышали о постигших его ___, они отправились в путь.
cases.translation: When the three friends heard of the misfortunes that had come upon him, they set out on a journey.
cases.explain: The preposition 'о' (about) governs the prepositional case in plural form.

reading.ru: Сатана ответил Господу, 'Я скитался по земле и обошел ее всю.'
reading.question: What did Satan say he had been doing?
options: Wandering on earth and walking back and forth on it
Tempting people to sin and leading them away from God
Observing the righteous and planning their downfall
Gathering an army to challenge God's authority
reading.correct: Wandering on earth and walking back and forth on it
reading.explain: Satan's own words: 'Я скитался по земле и обошел ее всю' (I have been wandering on earth and walking back and forth on it).

reading.ru: Разве даром Иов боится Бога? Разве не ты оградил его самого, его домашних и все его добро?
reading.question: What did Satan suggest about Job's fear of God?
options: Job fears God only because of God's protection and blessings
Job is naturally righteous and fears God out of genuine faith
Job's faith is a test of his family's commitment
Job fears God because he lacks courage for rebellion
reading.correct: Job fears God only because of God's protection and blessings
reading.explain: Satan's argument: 'Разве даром Иов боится Бога?' (Does not Job fear God for nothing?) and 'Разве не ты оградил его...?' (Have you not hedged him about?) implying that Job's fear is based on material blessings.

reading.ru: Жена сказала ему, 'Ты все еще держишься за свою непорочность? Прокляни Бога и умри.'
reading.question: What did Job's wife urge him to do?
options: Curse God and die rather than continue suffering
Accept his suffering as a test of faith and endure
Flee with her to another land to escape punishment
Offer a great sacrifice to appease God's anger
reading.correct: Curse God and die rather than continue suffering
reading.explain: The text explicitly shows her urging: 'Прокляни Бога и умри' (Curse God and die).

reading.ru: Он ответил ей, 'Ты говоришь как безумное. Разве мы должны принимать от Бога только хорошее и не принимать плохого?'
reading.question: How did Job respond to his wife's urging?
options: He said they should accept both good and evil from God
He agreed they should curse God but do it in secret
He blamed her for not understanding God's will
He said they should leave their home to escape judgment
reading.correct: He said they should accept both good and evil from God
reading.explain: Job's response: 'Разве мы должны принимать от Бога только хорошее и не принимать плохого?' (Shall we accept good from God and not accept evil?).

reading.ru: Когда трое друзей Иова, Элифас из Тимана, Билдад из Шуаха и Цафар из Наамы услышали о постигших его бедах, они отправились в путь, покинув свои дома.
reading.question: What did Job's three friends do when they heard of his troubles?
options: They left their homes and traveled to be with him
They sent him letters of sympathy but remained at home
They organized a sacrificial feast to pray for his recovery
They hired messengers to bring him food and supplies
reading.correct: They left their homes and traveled to be with him
reading.explain: The text states: 'они отправились в путь, покинув свои дома' (they set out on a journey, having left their homes).

reading.ru: Они сидели рядом с ним на земле семь дней и семь ночей, никто из них не сказал ему ни слова, потому что они видели, как сильно он страдает.
reading.question: How did Job's friends show their compassion during his suffering?
options: They sat with him in silence for seven days and nights because of his great suffering
They spoke encouraging words to him throughout their visit
They prepared healing remedies and applied them daily
They performed rituals to try to drive away his afflictions
reading.correct: They sat with him in silence for seven days and nights because of his great suffering
reading.explain: The text shows: 'Они сидели рядом с ним на земле семь дней и семь ночей, никто из них не сказал ему ни слова, потому что они видели, как сильно он страдает' (They sat beside him on the ground for seven days and seven nights, and no one said a word to him, for they saw how great was his suffering).
